from itertools import combinations
A=[[0.,.5,-.5],[-.5,0.,.5],[.5,-.5,0.]]

    vals=[]

strengths: Addresses an important optimization class with applications to sparse PCA, nonnegative PCA, and nonlinear eigenvalue problems.
The orthogonal row-block update correctly preserves XᵀX and applies to rectangular Stiefel matrices. Reducing two-row updates to rotations and reflections is a useful computational design.

The experiments cover four problem families, ten datasets, and multiple ranks and regularization parameters, with substantial reported objective improvements on several settings and relevant comparisons including ManPG and OptM.
weaknesses: The central stationarity claim in Theorem 5.5 is false under the stated assumptions. Consider n=r=3, X=I, f(X)=⟨A,X⟩ with A=[[0,0.5,-0.5],[-0.5,0,0.5],[0.5,-0.5,0]], and the convex row-separable function h(X)=Σ_i|Σ_j X_ij−1|. With Q=0, every two-row exact subproblem is minimized by I₂, yet the feasible curve exp(−tA) has objective derivative −1.5 at t=0. Thus an exact BS₂ point need not be critical. Appendix B.8 incorrectly turns the existence of a suitable subgradient for each block into the existence of one subgradient satisfying every block simultaneously.

The strong-convergence proof has independent substantive errors. Equation (56), step ②, exchanges Bᵗ and Bᵗ⁺¹ despite Xᵗ⁺¹ depending on Bᵗ. Lemma 6.6(b) also incorrectly converts a root-mean-square residual bound into a mean-residual bound: for n=3, r=1, k=2, h=0, f(x)=x₂, and x=e₁, its left side is 1 while its right side is √(2/3). These errors invalidate the presented proof of Theorem 6.8.

The exact breakpoint solver in Section 7.1 is incorrect as written. The substitution t=tan(θ) omits cos(θ)=0, which can contain global minimizers. Discarding coordinates with y_i=0 is also invalid for the ℓ₁ penalty: when x_i≠0, their contribution λ|x_i|/√(1+t²) depends on t. Consequently, the claimed exact subproblem solution is not guaranteed.

The experimental description contains a consequential feasibility inconsistency. Section 9.1 initializes nonnegative PCA with X(G_i,i)=1/|G_i|, giving column squared norm 1/|G_i| rather than 1. Since OBCD preserves the Gram matrix, this initialization cannot yield the reported near-machine-precision feasibility. The implementation must be reconciled with the stated procedure; the correct normalization is 1/√|G_i|.

The evaluation does not adequately isolate algorithmic superiority. Only the proposed breakpoint routine uses C++, and the baseline-plus-OBCD experiments receive ten additional seconds without an equal-budget baseline-continuation control. Baseline tuning, preprocessing, stopping tolerances, random seeds, and variability across repeated runs are insufficiently documented. Additional objective reduction alone does not establish stronger stationarity.

The demonstrated scope is narrower than the broad claims: all experiments use k=2 and n≤1000, without convincing scaling studies or ablations isolating reflections and exact subproblem optimization. Assumption 6.1 also excludes unbounded subdifferentials encountered at zeros for ℓ₀ penalties and at boundaries for nonnegativity indicators, limiting the strong-convergence coverage of headline applications.
